narrative:
The 2023 Kansas City Royals were a team in the midst of a painful rebuild, finishing 56-106 — one of the worst records in franchise history. From the very first game of the season, the Royals were outmatched, going 7-21 in April and setting the tone for a long summer. Their pitching staff posted a bloated 5.17 ERA, and the bullpen in particular surrendered gut-punch moments all year long, with Scott Barlow repeatedly appearing in the wrong kind of highlight reel.

The few bright spots belonged almost entirely to the franchise's core pieces. Salvador Perez continued to be the heartbeat of the lineup, delivering clutch home runs when the team desperately needed life. And a young Bobby Witt Jr. flashed his immense potential, including a grand slam in late July that briefly reminded fans what this team could one day become. Freddy Fermin also had his moments, particularly a walk-off-style double in late June that provided one of the summer's rare feel-good memories.

The season's bleakest stretch came through August, when the Royals lost 19 of 28 games. Carlos Hernández gave up multiple crushing home runs in a brutal three-week span, and the team's playoff dreams — however faint they may have been — were fully extinguished. Losses piled up against Seattle, Pittsburgh, and the Mets, each one a reminder of how far Kansas City still had to go to compete.

September offered a merciful reprieve and a glimpse of the future, with the Royals posting a 14-13 record in their final full month — their only winning month of the season. Bobby Witt Jr. and Drew Waters contributed highlight-reel moments, and the team played with a looseness that hinted at better days ahead. It wasn't enough to change the story of 2023, but it was enough to keep hope alive heading into the offseason.

chapters.title: Sinking Fast
chapters.description: The Royals open the year with early flashes of offense but fall apart quickly, going a dismal 7-21 in April.

chapters.title: Treading Water
chapters.description: May and early June bring marginal improvement as Michael Massey and Salvador Perez deliver clutch moments, but the team can't string wins together.

chapters.title: Summer Swings
chapters.description: Late June produces a few memorable highlights — including Freddy Fermin's clutch double — even as the Royals limp through another losing month.

chapters.title: Bobby's Grand Statement
chapters.description: Bobby Witt Jr.'s grand slam in late July stands as the season's signature moment of promise amid another difficult stretch.

chapters.title: August Agony
chapters.description: A brutal August sees Carlos Hernández surrender multiple crushing home runs as the Royals lose 19 of 28 and the season fully unravels.

chapters.title: September's Silver Lining
chapters.description: The Royals close the year with their only winning month, as Witt Jr. and Drew Waters provide late-season highlights and a reason for optimism.
